grim_examples: GRIM validation examples are the published ones from the scrutiny reference manual (Brown & Heathers 2017 method): grim(x='5.19', n=28) is inconsistent, grim(x='5.19', n=32) is consistent. GRIMMER core is validated against a brute-force enumeration of actual integer datasets in the test suite (an achieved (mean, SD, N) triple may never be flagged) plus hand-verified arithmetic cases documented in the tests.
purpose: A recorded statcheck output (Spec 008) in statcheck's data-frame-as-CSV shape, built exclusively from classifications the statcheck project itself asserts in its public test suite, plus the GRIM/GRIMMER published worked examples cited in the test module. No row was produced by running statcheck in this project (no R runtime exists in this environment).

rows.grounding: The twelve result strings in tests/testthat/test-decisionerror.R of MicheleNuijten/statcheck ('simple decision errors are classified as such'), each asserted expect_true(...[[VAR_DEC_ERROR]]). decision_error=TRUE is the project's own assertion; error=TRUE follows because a decision error is by definition also an inconsistency.

The five result strings in tests/testthat/test-compute-pvalues.R, where the project asserts the computed p-value equals R's pt/pf/pnorm/pchisq formulas. computed_p here was evaluated from those same formulas; decision_error=FALSE because reported and computed p lie on the same side of alpha=.05 in each row; error=TRUE because the computed p, rounded to the reported precision, differs from the reported p in each row (statcheck's published definition of an inconsistency).

't(28) = 2.20, p = .05' is asserted expect_false(...[[VAR_DEC_ERROR]]) under default arguments in the pEqualAlphaSig section of test-decisionerror.R. error=TRUE by the rounding definition (computed 0.036225 rounds to .04, not .05).

txt1 of the exact-statistics section of test-decisionerror.R: the t value is qt(.04/2, 28, lower.tail=FALSE) by construction (computed_p exactly .04) and the classification is asserted expect_false for both error-relevant outcomes; the t value recorded here (2.1539348677) is that quantile, evaluated by bisection on the t CDF and verified against published critical values.
